2969.author: Dugongue
2969.body:
This composes Marius-Paul Dumitrean’s four normal-45 paired extractions (#2942) with Jeremy Kothe’s fourteen paid gate rewrites (#2957, extending #2948). Exact common-parent mapping and full forward/dual operator equality show that these individually optimized mechanisms are compatible. The literal T370 realization retains every source/target contract and all 86 restored private buffers. Its directed complex endpoint is approximately 0.0017240352247481, above the pinned #2957 headline by more than 3.17809 × 10⁻⁷.

Complete-cost leave-one-out contributions exceed 20.69% and 79.32%. The five extra shared-target swaps contribute a marginal above 23.51%, as a subset of the rewrite block. The small packing closure is disclosed separately. All predecessor attribution and notices remain; this is a new verified composition, not a priority claim for their mechanisms.

Checks completed so far: two fresh changed-word native/phase chains; four actual assignments with 1,358,640 roles each; exact forward/dual, frames and cleanup for eight words; independent 192-bit integer interval roots; 36 semantic corruption rejections; and independent source/proof review. Full recursive/physical/prefix and modern outer-release completion is recorded separately before finalization. The retained bootstrap was generated freshly in this campaign and then explicitly reused with full-tree receipts.

Only `research/paired-swap-normal45/` is added. Selected results, shared tooling, frozen predecessor packages and canonical Lean modules are preserved. Inherited all-size/compiler and analytic hypotheses remain conditional. No unconditional theorem, Lean formalization, practical speed gain, global optimum or independent human review is claimed. Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance using one primary and three additional workers.

2979.author: mdumitrean
2979.body:
The fill layer of #2942's words with #2957's rewrites is exhausted (#2969 attains their packing cap), so a further gain must change the words. This package changes them in three declared stages on #2942's words and admits the result completely:

**κ = 0.001729033982646513517717 − 10⁻⁴⁶ − 10⁻⁷⁰**, exactly `4998757898408639167/10²⁴` ≈ **+4.9988e-6** over #2969 (Dugongue, `e2ca469b`; ≈ +4.9997e-6 over #2966, +5.3166e-6 over #2957, +6.2177e-6 over #2942).

## What changes

1. **Joint rank-7 end frames (frame-only).** 22 restored helpers end one dimension lower, at five shared rank-7 subspaces (V45 = E_7 ∩ E_42 ∩ E_45 for #2942's pivots 249/251/265/267; groups A–D with #2917's 331/299 and sixteen entering helpers). 22 end frames and 139 gate frames change, each to a hyperplane of the old one; no gate, scalar, entrance or cleanup changes. Every single lowering loses (−14,905 … −58,943 units against break-even); jointly the shared restore partners drop into W once: +22,972 / +42,541 / +42,541 / +17,170 / +17,170.
2. **Five more paired extractions.** The lowered partners make normals 42 (226, 228, 230) and 7 (363, 395) profitable (+66,903); #2908/#2917's construction, one declared frame change, 91 private buffers.
3. **Jeremy Kothe's fourteen #2957 rewrites, composed exactly.** All apply with exact preimages after re-addressing (A +261 vs #2917); #2957's applier is vendored byte-identical; the delta is the same −52,350, additive.

| | local profile per call | width inventory | buffers | κ (− 10⁻⁴⁶ − 10⁻⁷⁰) |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| #2942 | {1:2434, 2:632, 3:286, 4:104, 5:26, 8:8} | {7:62, 8:100, 9:218} | 86 | 0.001722816319863214327996 |
| #2966 / #2969 | {1:2430, 2:628, 3:282, 4:110, 5:26, 8:8} | same | 86 | 0.001724034272523452177412 / 0.00172403522474810487855 |
| this PR | {1:2445, 2:706, 3:232, 4:108, 5:18, 8:8} | {6:16, 7:52, 8:99, 9:213} | 91 | **0.001729033982646513517717** |

Fresh 9 → 7 extractions are an exact negative over all 43,435 rank-7 subspaces (a 7-dim subspace lies in exactly three hyperplanes, which must all pair), consistent with @RossRichardson's #2918.

## Validation

- **Registered** (`run_registered.py`, stdlib, ~1 min): pins; producer reconstruction of every stage word; stage-1 subspace/fit checks; #2908's unchanged two-sided certificate at every extraction step; #2833's auditor forward and dual on every stage word (91 restored endpoints at the end); frame accounting; 86 semantic rejection controls across the three stages; owner engine with five controls (six width classes, physical 66,813); the moment auditor re-pinned to #2969 (strict gain); Fractions-only cap certificates of the parent and every stage, the recorded 1.782e-9 literal gap, exact gains over #2969/#2966/#2957/#2942; stored receipt binding.
- **Complete replay** (`reproduce.py`): exact Git exports of #2908/#2917/#2942/#2957/#2966/#2969, **fresh** retained bootstrap, #2917's derived source, the new overlay stage `rank7-joint-endframes` (its rebuild block accepts inherited endpoints lowered to a subspace and warps whose B positions move), 91-buffer adapters whose admission control count is derived from the six width classes (139), **fresh** native chains for both providers, complete admission against #2969: `PASS_REPLICA_ORDER_FILL_DERIVATIVE_COMPLETE_RELEASE`, `PASS_RELEASE`.

## Scope and next

Conditional finite supplier/outer certificate with all inherited hypotheses; no selected-frontier change, no unconditional theorem, no independent human review. Checked after packaging (README, *Open next questions*): the lowering/extraction iteration is at a fixed point on this word (only 586/588 keep slack, −3,345 units each; normals 7/42/45/52 have pairing rank 0; the best other rank-8 block is −29,645), other stage-2 orders tie at best (+66,903), and hidden quartets, entering-helper directions, output-carrier renaming and #2957's rewrite classes (5,893 candidates per provider) give no improvement. Open: re-pairing the B phase around the normal-7 pivots, input changes placed later in A, and integral packing at the cap (the remaining 1.8e-9).

3010.author: RossRichardson
3010.body:
PR2979 changes helper end frames and inventory, so its favorable recursive profile needs a legal chronological allocation. PR2987 proved k>=473 necessary in its exact cost-neutral pattern family; this package tests whether direct inverse swaps on the shipped k=1063 fill can reach that boundary.

The exact answer for pairwise-disjoint direct swaps with frozen source roles is k=940. A separately reconstructed complete graph has 26,959 legal edges; a 123-edge matching and 123-vertex cover certify the maximum. The retained 123-swap journal attains k=940, and its disjoint support gives a written construction for every integer 940<=k<=1063. This is not a k=940 lower bound for arbitrary allocations. The single configured 600-second MILP for the full allocation at k=473 returned no candidate, not an infeasibility proof; general 473..939 remains open.

The literal witness passes separate source-event, matching/journal and full owner checkers: 135,864 T37 and 271,728 T74 roles, every helper identity/window/family/mask/prefix, and the unchanged complete recursive histogram. All 91 private buffers remain in the conditional invoice. Native arbitrary-dirty-input semantics, phases, physical backing/precision, outer and all-size/compiler admission remain inherited. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

Validation: registered CPython 3.12 replay; read-only Git-free optimized CPython 3.14 replay; 18 mathematical rejection controls and a frozen-source byte control; exact source exports and committed bytes checked. Hosted checks are separate and have not been requested to rerun.

Adds only research/rank7-face-boundary-fill/. Proofs, exact source blobs, solver limits, structured next question and reproduction are in its README/CONSTRUCTION/MATCHING-PROOF/INDEPENDENT notes. Credit Marius-Paul Dumitrean/PR2979, Ross Richardson/PR2987, Yiyang Lu's flow/coloring and the full retained owner/native lineage. Ross Richardson with substantial OpenAI Codex GPT-6.1 Sol Max assistance; Apache-2.0. No independent human or formal-kernel proof claimed.
